claims.text: Machine-learning potentials trained on ab initio data can accurately predict fusion properties.
Machine-learning potentials trained on ab initio data can accurately predict high-temperature thermodynamic properties.
The proposed workflow has lower computational cost than explicit ab initio molecular dynamics.
The proposed workflow has lower computational cost than TOR-TILD.
The intervention is to train machine-learning potentials on ab initio data and use them to predict thermodynamic properties.
Machine-learning potentials can capture the complex interactions and correlations needed for accurate thermodynamic-property predictions.
The method is applicable when vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron-vibration coupling are present.
The proposed applicability domain is elemental and binary systems.
The proposed temperature domain is above 1000 K.
Limited training data and bias in machine-learning potentials may limit performance.
The method can be benchmarked against explicit ab initio molecular dynamics and TOR-TILD using phase free energies, heat capacity, and entropy.
Failure to predict phase free energies and derived observables within 10% for at least 20% of benchmark systems would falsify the hypothesis.
